description: Get the top co-occurring words and phrases from TV news clips matching a query — the vocabulary framing a topic on television. Returns the most frequent non-stopword terms with relative frequency scores (0–100, where 100 = the query term itself). Terms and scores come from GDELT's relevance-ranked sample of matching clips, documented as the 200 most relevant, not all matching coverage — compare windows or stations with a separate, narrower call for each. Use to understand narrative framing, identify related concepts mentioned alongside a topic, or generate follow-up search terms. Returns 25 terms by default, with count pages up to 25,000 terms. Archive coverage varies by station; check gdelt_list_tv_stations for each station’s monitoring date range.

endDatetime.description: End datetime in GDELT format YYYYMMDDHHMMSS — exactly 14 digits, no separators (e.g. 20200131235959). Must pair with startDatetime; supplying only one of the two is rejected.

limit.description: Maximum score-sorted terms returned per page (default 25, cap 25,000). Larger counts clamp with limitClamp; strict deployments reject them.

offset.description: Zero-based term offset in descending score order. Use nextOffset with the same query inputs for the next page.

query.description: Search query for TV transcript content. Same TV operators as gdelt_search_tv: station:CNN, network:CBS, market:"National", show:"Anderson Cooper", context:"vaccine".

startDatetime.description: Start datetime in GDELT format YYYYMMDDHHMMSS — exactly 14 digits, no separators (e.g. 20200101000000). Must pair with endDatetime; supplying only one of the two is rejected. Check station monitoring dates with gdelt_list_tv_stations.

stations.description: Station IDs to filter to (e.g. ["CNN", "FOXNEWS"]) — the stationId values gdelt_list_tv_stations returns, not display labels such as "FOX News". Alternatively use station:, network:, or quoted market: selectors in query; a selector is required. Obtain network and market values and per-station archive ranges from gdelt_list_tv_stations.

timespan.description: Relative window counting back from now (a number and unit such as d, m, or y). Now is past the end of most stations' monitoring, so for archived periods set startDatetime/endDatetime inside a station's range from gdelt_list_tv_stations. Ignored when startDatetime/endDatetime are set.

name: gdelt_get_tv_context

effectiveQuery.description: Echoed query string for use in follow-up calls.

error.description: Present when the call failed. Absent on success.

code.description: JSON-RPC error code for this failure.

reason.description: Machine-readable failure mode. Declared by this tool: `offset_out_of_range`: The requested term offset is at or beyond the end of a non-empty result. `invalid_date_range`: Only one of startDatetime / endDatetime was supplied, one of them is not a real UTC calendar timestamp, or startDatetime is not earlier than endDatetime. `invalid_query`: A stations entry is not a station ID, GDELT rejected the query — no station was selected, or the query string is malformed — or the TV timespan is malformed. `gdelt_rate_limited`: GDELT rejected the request for its one-request-per-five-seconds limit, or too many requests were already queued for this one to start in time. `gdelt_unavailable`: GDELT TV API is unreachable or temporarily returned no usable data. Other values are possible when a failure originates below the handler.

recovery.description: Actionable next step for the caller.

message.description: Human-readable description of what went wrong.

limitClamp.description: Present only when the requested count exceeded the per-call cap: the call ran exactly as a call at the cap, and every count, notice, and continuation in this response reflects the applied value.

applied.description: The per-call cap the call ran with instead.

parameter.description: The count input that was clamped.

requested.description: The value the call asked for.

nextOffset.description: Offset of the next term page; absent on the final page.

notice.description: On every non-empty result, that terms and scores come from GDELT's relevance-ranked sample of matching clips, documented as the 200 most relevant, not all matching coverage — compare windows or stations with a separate, narrower call for each. When no clips matched, so there is no vocabulary to report: the resolved timespan window; for each selected station whose monitoring range the window misses, that range and how to search inside it; and how to broaden the query or check station monitoring dates.

offset.description: Zero-based offset of this term page.

staleResponse.description: Present only when the refetch of this exact request was refused, failed, or came back empty, and the response is GDELT's stored answer from fetchedAt instead. It holds nothing published after fetchedAt; a relative timespan covers the window ending at fetchedAt, not now. Absent on a live answer.

ageSeconds.description: Age of the stored answer when served, in whole seconds.

fetchedAt.description: ISO 8601 time GDELT returned the stored answer.

reason.description: Why the refetch was not used: GDELT rate-limited it, did not answer with data, or answered empty — which GDELT also does under load.

totalTerms.description: Total co-occurring terms before pagination; never a clip count.

truncated.description: True when more terms remain after this page; use nextOffset to retrieve them.

words.description: Co-occurring terms from GDELT's relevance-ranked sample of matching clips, documented as the 200 most relevant, not all matching coverage, sorted by score descending.

items.description: A co-occurring term with its relative frequency score.

score.description: Relative frequency score (0–100). The query term itself scores 100; other terms are proportional to their co-occurrence frequency within GDELT's relevance-ranked sample of matching clips, documented as the 200 most relevant, not all matching coverage.

title: Get GDELT TV Context
